current_example.title: Example: Calculating the Lateral Surface Area of a Cube Given its Dimensions

q-86336.name: Question 1
q-86336.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250845/assets/5eef04daa0a8ac1a590b3a0da378d9184ad9b82c5e4834c5079ccb4f3665cced.png)

Determine the surface area for the cube above.
q-86336.worked_solution:
The surface area $S$ of a cube can be found using the formula

$$
S=6{s}^{2},
$$

where $s$ is the side length of the cube.

Substituting $s=2\sqrt{5}\,\text{cm}$ into the formula, we get 

$$
S=6(2\sqrt{5}\,\text{cm})^{2}=120\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.
$$

$$
S=6{s}^{2},

q-23926.name: Question 3
q-23926.problem: The surface area of a cube is $150$ square units. Find the length of the edges of the cube.
q-23926.worked_solution:
The surface area $S$ of a cube is made up of $6$ congruent squares. So, the area $A$ of one face is

$$
A=\frac{S}{6}=\frac{150}{6}=25\,.
$$

Since $A={s}^{2},$ where $s$ is the length of an edge, we can find $s$ as follows:

$$
s=\sqrt{A}=\sqrt{25}=5
$$

Therefore, the length of the edges is $5$ units.

q-86353.name: Question 4
q-86353.problem: The surface area of a cube is $294\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.$ Find the length of the edges of the cube.
q-86353.worked_solution:
The surface area $S$ of a cube is made up of $6$ congruent squares. So, the area $A$ of one face is

$$
A=\frac{S}{6}=\frac{294}{6}=49\,{\text{cm}}^{2}\,.
$$

Since $A={s}^{2},$ where $s$ is the length of an edge, we can find $s$ as follows:

$$
s=\sqrt{A}=\sqrt{49}=7\,\text{cm}
$$

Therefore, the length of the edges is $7\,\text{cm}.$

q-107341.worked_solution:

q-118510.name: Question 6
q-118510.problem: The lateral surface area of a cube is $400\,{\text{ft}}^{2}.$ Find the length of the edges of the cube.
q-118510.worked_solution:
The lateral surface area ${S}_{L}$ of a cube is made up of $4$ congruent squares. So, the area $A$ of one face is

$$
A=\frac{{S}_{L}}{4}=\frac{400}{4}=100\,{\text{ft}}^{2}\,.
$$

Since $A={s}^{2},$ where $s$ is the length of an edge, we can find $s$ as follows:

$$
s=\sqrt{A}=\sqrt{100}=10\,\text{ft}
$$

Therefore, the length of the edges is $10\,\text{ft}.$
